title: Kardashian family
description: American family prominent in entertainment, business, and fashion
wiki_lead:
The Kardashian family ( kar-DASH-ee-ən), also referred to as the Kardashian–Jenner family, is an American family prominent in the fields of entertainment, reality television, fashion design, and business. Through different ventures, several members of the family have assets of over $1 billion.
The patriarch of the family was American attorney Robert Kardashian (1944–2021), who gained notoriety for being one of O. J. Simpson's lawyers during the O. J. Simpson murder case in 1994. The family reached greater recognition in 2007, after Kardashian's middle daughter, Kim Kardashian, was involved in the pornographic film Kim Kardashian, Superstar, which featured her then-boyfriend Ray J, catapulting the family into the world of reality television and business. From 2007 to 2021, the Kardashian–Jenner family appeared together on the highly popular, albeit controversial, reality television show Keeping Up with the Kardashians. The show's 14-year run gave and maintained media exposure to each member of the family, allowing them to start and build their individual careers in multiple businesses under their separate brands.
Kardashian and first wife Kris Jenner (née Houghton) had four children: Kourtney (b. 1979), Kim (b. 1980), Khloé (b. 1984), and Rob Kardashian (b. 1987). After Robert and Kris divorced in 1991, she remarried to Olympic decathlon champion Bruce Jenner (known since 2015 as Caitlyn Jenner). They had two daughters: Kendall and Kylie Jenner. Robert died of esophageal cancer in 2003. Notable extended relatives include Brandon and Brody Jenner, the half-siblings of Kendall and Kylie (through Bruce/Caitlyn's marriage to Linda Thompson); Scott Disick, the longtime boyfriend of Kourtney Kardashian, with whom she shares three children; Travis Barker, Blink-182 drummer and husband of Kourtney, whom she shares one child with; rapper Kanye West, former husband to Kim Kardashian and father to their four children together; Canadian basketball player Tristan Thompson, former boyfriend of Khloé and father to their two children; model Blac Chyna, former girlfriend of Rob and mother to their one child; rapper and singer Travis Scott, former boyfriend of Kylie and father to their two children.
They have since been referred to as "America's most famous family" by Glamour, "one of the most influential family 'dynasties' in the world" by Insider, and the biggest influencers of the 2010s by Vogue. They are the focus of the book Kardashian Dynasty: The Controversial Rise of America's Royal Family by Ian Halperin.
The family is best known for their longest-running reality television show, Keeping Up with the Kardashians (2007–2021). Spin-offs included: Kourtney and Kim Take Miami (2009–2013); Kourtney and Khloé Take Miami (2009–2013); Kourtney and Kim Take New York (2011–2012); Khloé & Lamar (2013); Kourtney and Kim Take Miami (2014–2015); Kourtney and Khloé Take The Hamptons (2014–2015); Dash Dolls (2015) and Life of Kylie (2017). In 2022, the family debuted their new reality television series The Kardashians.

Spin-offs included: Kourtney and Kim Take Miami (2009–2013); Kourtney and Khloé Take Miami (2009–2013); Kourtney and Kim Take New York (2011–2012); Khloé & Lamar (2013); Kourtney and Kim Take Miami (2014–2015); Kourtney and Khloé Take The Hamptons (2014–2015); Dash Dolls (2015) and Life of Kylie (2017). In 2022, the family debuted their new reality television series The Kardashians.


Family background

Robert Kardashian Sr. was the son of Helen and Arthur Kardashian. All four of his grandparents were Armenian who emigrated from the Ottoman Empire to the United States of America in the early 20th century, originating from the provinces of Kars and Ardahan in modern-day Turkey. The family left the Ottoman Empire before the Armenian genocide began in 1915.


History
In 1978, American attorney Robert Kardashian (1944–2003) married Kristen "Kris" Houghton (now Kris Jenner). During their 13-year marriage, they had four children: Kourtney Mary Kardashian (b. 1979), Kimberly Noel Kardashian (b. 1980), Khloé Alexandra Kardashian (b. 1984), and Robert Arthur Kardashian (b. 1987). Robert Kardashian's roots are of Armenian descent, while Kris is of Dutch, English, Irish, German and Scottish descent. Kardashian filed for divorce from Kris in 1990, after discovering infidelities on her behalf; the divorce was finalized in 1991. 
Kardashian met then-rising football player O. J. Simpson at a tennis court around 1969. Kris was introduced to Simpson's then-girlfriend Nicole Brown through Kardashian when she was 17. Soon after, the couples developed a very close friendship, with Kris describing them as family. After Brown was murdered in 1994, Simpson was charged with of her murder, as well as her friend Ron Goldman. Kardashian joined Simpson's legal team in the highly publicized murder trial the same year, for which he gained subsequent notoriety.
In the month following the Kardashian's divorce finalization, Kris married her second husband, former Olympian Bruce Jenner. Soon after the murder trial concluded in January 1995, the Jenners became pregnant with their first child, Kendall Nicole Jenner (b. 1995), whose middle name is a tribute to Brown. Jenner gave birth to her sixth and youngest child, Kylie Kristen Jenner in 1997.
In 2006, Kris Jenner developed a concept for a reality series revolving around her family; the idea was catapulted following the release of her daughter Kim's sex tape, Kim Kardashian, Superstar, in March 2007 by Vivid Entertainment. With the backing of Ryan Seacrest and his production company, Keeping Up with the Kardashians was created, premiering on the E! Network in October of 2007. The series ran from 2007 to 2020 during its 20-season-tenure, becoming one of E!'s most successful reality shows, along with its many spin-offs.


Business


Fashion
In 2003, Kris Jenner and her eldest daughter Kourtney opened the children's clothing boutique Smooch, which operated for six years before closing in 2009. In 2006, sisters Kourtney, Kim, and Khloé Kardashian opened their high-end women's clothing boutique DASH in Calabasas, California. The three sisters would extend the chain to Miami Beach in 2009, New York City in 2010, and West Hollywood in 2012. The chain ceased its operations in 2018. The sisters would continue their fashion expansion with their K-DASH by Kardashian line for QVC, which launched in September 2010.
In 2011, the Kardashian sisters signed a deal with department store Sears to launch the Kardashian Kollection, a clothing, handbag, and accessory collection. The sisters partnered with Australian designer Bruno Schiavi's Jupi International to create the collection. Announced in August, the collection launched in September in 700 Sears locations as Executive Vice President of Apparel and Home Accessories John Goodman described the project as vital to reinventing Sears' apparel and image. The line later extended to Kardashian Kollection Home, which sold bedding and home decor, and expand internationally in 2012, partnering with Arcadia Group chairman Sir Philip Green for the collection to be sold in over 250 locations of the British women's clothing retailer Dorothy Perkins, as well as 11 other countries in the Middle East and Asia. With a quickly sold out collaboration with Lipsy in 2013, the collection reached substantial success before being discontinued in May 2015.


Body and beauty
In 2010, the Kardashian sisters launched the Kardashian Beauty line, with their first product being their tanning gel, Kardashian Glamour Tan, which was sold exclusively at Sephora. Subsequently, PerfectSkin, the sisters' skincare product, was introduced to the line. In June 2012, the Kardashian sisters announced the launch of their makeup collection, Khroma Beauty, which was later rebranded to Kardashian Beauty after a lengthy legal battle with a company of a similar name.


Finance
Briefly in November 2010, the Kardashian sisters partnered with credit card company Mastercard to produce the Kardashian Kard, a pre-paid credit card. The partnership dissolved after three weeks due to high fees for ATM withdrawals and cancellations, which could reach $100 a year.


Authorship
Collectively, Kourtney, Kim, and Khloé Kardashian have published two books, their first being the shared autobiography Kardashian Konfidential (2010), which, at its peak, reached No. 3 on The New York Times Best Sellers list in the "Advice, How-To, and Miscellaneous" category, and remained on the list for five weeks from December 2010 to January 2011. In May 2011, Kim announced to her Celebuzz blog that the sisters were writing their first fiction book with William Morrow and Company, as the sisters enlisted the help of their fans with naming the book. Dollhouse (2011) was released on November 15.
In 2014, Kendall and Kylie Jenner jointly published their dystopian fiction novel, Rebels: City of Indra: The Story of Lex and Livia. The book received criticism due to the Jenner sisters' use of ghostwriter Maya Sloan. As Rebels ended on a cliffhanger, the Jenner sisters published the series' second installment, Time of the Twins, in 2016.


Reception
The family and media give Kim the credit for helping them start their careers. The family has been criticized as being famous for being famous. Ben Hecht, writing in 1954, pointed out that "People in our day become famous who are no more than advertisements, and they advertise not genius but existence. They are famous for stopping at hotels, for holding hands in public, for speaking to each other, for having babies, for getting invited to parties ... We are less interested in their talents than in their publicized routines." In late May 2020, Forbes released an investigation into Kylie's finances, alleging she misrepresented her billionaire status. Writers Chase Peterson-Withorn and Madeline Berg stated, "... white lies, omissions and outright fabrications are to be expected from the family that perfected—then monetized—the concept of 'famous for being famous.'" Vogue stated the Kardashians have "... proved that although they were 'famous for being famous' in the 2000s, in the 2010s they became a cultural force to be reckoned with." They were given keys to Beverly Hills on September 2, 2010, the date (written as 9/02/10) intentionally selected to match the area's ZIP Code of 90210. The family are often criticized for blackfishing and cultural appropriation of African-American culture.


Parodies
The Kardashians have inspired a number of parodies, including on the television sketch comedy Saturday Night Live, on which Kim Kardashian has appeared multiple times. The YouTube animated parody channel Simgm Productions has also gained popularity for their parodies of numerous celebrities and media franchises, including the Kardashian's, through the use of animation and characters in the Sims. Other popular adult animated series, such as Family Guy, The Simpsons and South Park have also depicted and parodied the Kardashians.
